events.title: Campfire Program - Nocturnal Wildlife
events.description:
Join MTRP Park Ranger Brandon Botticelli for a campfire program at the scenic Lake Amphitheater in Kumeyaay Lake Campground.  Join in singing some familiar songs as the campfire flames begin to flicker and cast a glow over the area.  Trail Guide Linda Stafford will then present a program on nocturnal wildlife.  Learn the fascinating stories of animals after dark.  Nature always surprises!

This program is free with no reservations required.  Please park in the dirt lot at the corner of Father Junipero Serra Trail and Bushy Hill Dr. across from the campground.  Walk into the campground and follow the road past the entry station around to the short Lake Amphitheater trail at campsite #10.  Mosquitoes are likely so take precautions.
events.location: Kumeyaay Lake Campground (2 Father Junipero Serra Trail, San Diego, CA 92119, United States)

events.title: Guided Nature Walk from the Visitor Center
events.description:
Join an MTRP Trail Guide on a special Presidents Day nature walk and learn about the plants, animals, geology, history, and ecology of the park on one of these scenic trails:

  *   The Oak Grove Loop showcasing majestic coast live oaks and rare Engelmann’s oaks.
  *   The Visitor Center Loop highlighting coastal sage scrub, chaparral, and riparian woodland habitats.
  *   The Riverside Grinding Rocks featuring one of the archaeological sites in the park.

These interpretive nature walks are offered to enhance your appreciation of the unique beauty of San Diego’s natural environment.  The park is constantly changing, so see and learn new things on walks throughout the year.
Walks start from the Visitor Center every Saturday, Sunday, and Wednesday at 9:30 a.m.  Walks are free and open to the public, with no reservations required.
The trails used are easy, but have uneven surfaces and some involve steps, so be sure to wear sturdy, closed-toe shoes and bring along water.  A hat and sunscreen are also recommended.  Walks are canceled if raining.
events.location: Mission Trails Regional Park Visitor Center (1 Father Junipero Serra Trl, San Diego, CA 92119, United States)

events.title: Reading with a Ranger
events.description:
Celebrate Latino Conservation Week at Mission Trails with a special Reading with a Ranger program presented in both English and Spanish.

City of San Diego Park Ranger Elizabeth Delgado will lead a family-friendly read-aloud designed to help young visitors connect with nature, wildlife and the park through storytelling. It’s a fun opportunity for children and families to spend time together, meet a park ranger and learn more about the natural world around them.

This program is free.

events.title: Bat Walk ***FULL***
events.description:
Attendance on this bat walk is limited to 40.  Register at https://forms.gle/ArhHS2Ljp9Htcz579
Join MTRP Trail Guides for free special interpretive bat walks at twilight this summer. Come and enjoy an evening walk in the park and learn about the species of bats commonly found in Mission Trails, their diet, and behavior.  Trail Guides trained as Bat Ambassadors will identify the species of bats using Echo Meter electronic devices.  Everyone will get a chance to see and hear bat chatter.  Don't forget to bring along a flashlight and an extra layer of clothing -- it often cools down after the sun sets.  This walk is not recommended for children 5 and under.  For more information, contact Ranger Monica Demetry at mdemetry@sandiego.gov<mailto:mdemtry@sandiego.gov>.
Upcoming Evening Walk:

  *   Saturday, September 20 at 6:15 p.m.

events.title: Guided Bird Walk - Kumeyaay Lake
events.description:
Description:

Join MTRP bird walk leaders for a guided bird walk along the shore of Kumeyaay Lake.  The fall months may yield some migratory warblers, sparrows, and waterfowl. Kumeyaay Lake often surprises us if we take the time to stop, look, and listen. This bird walk is designed for beginning or newer birdwatchers, but all skill levels are welcome to attend.

Bring binoculars if you have them.  Wear sturdy, closed-toe shoes, and bring along water.  A hat and sunscreen are also recommended.  Walks are canceled if raining.
